Derivative-Free Optimization 8: The Differential Evolution Minimisers¶

Differential evolution keeps a population of candidate points and improves it by recombination, using only function values. It is the method of choice when a function has many local minima and you can afford thousands of evaluations. Two standalone minimisers exist: differential_evolution_minimizer, the classic scheme, and differential_evolution_prmm_minimizer, a self-adapting variant. After this chapter you can run either directly, set its parameters on purpose, reproduce a run, and read how it stopped.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program. Counts are evaluations of the objective, and a “generation” is one pass over the population.

The method¶

Start with population_size points drawn over the box (or around the starting point if there are no bounds); the starting point is always one of them. In each generation, for each member:

  1. Build a mutant from three other members: one plus mutation_factor times the difference of two others. (best_mix moves the base of the mutant from a random member toward the best member.)

  2. Cross the mutant with the member: each coordinate comes from the mutant with probability crossover_rate, otherwise from the member.

  3. Keep the better of the member and the trial.

Because the step sizes come from the spread of the population itself, the method adapts its scale automatically: it takes large steps while the population is spread out and fine steps as it collapses on a minimum. That also means a population that collapses too early on the wrong minimum cannot recover. Population size and seed matter for this reason.

The calls¶

PopulationSolverOutcome differential_evolution_minimizer(objective, initial, DifferentialEvolutionConfig config = {});
PopulationSolverOutcome differential_evolution_prmm_minimizer(objective, initial, DifferentialEvolutionPrmmConfig config = {});

PopulationSolverOutcome holds minimizer, minimum, status (Converged, ReachedIterationBudget, ReachedEvaluationBudget) and diagnostics (iterations = generations, evaluations, last_step). The facade’s DfoOptions::differential_evolution and differential_evolution_prmm hold the same structures.

Programs¶

  • Differential evolution in practice

Checklist¶

  1. Give bounds; differential evolution is a global method and works best in a box.

  2. Set population_size to at least 5 to 10 times the number of variables, more for rugged functions.

  3. Set max_evaluations to what you can afford; leave check_every at 0 for multimodal problems, or turn it on when you know the function has one minimum.

  4. Fix rng_seed to reproduce a run; run several seeds to judge a multimodal result.

  5. When you cannot tune the parameters, use the self-adapting variant.
